newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 1996 current account surplus falls 30.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Japan 1996 current account surplus falls 30.9 pct.

text.p: The surplus in Japan's current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, shrank 30.9 percent to 7.1806 trillion yen in calendar 1996 from a year earlier, the Finance Ministry announced on Monday.
The surplus in merchandise trade alone fell 26.2 percent to 9.1152 trillion yen in 1996 from a year earlier.
The current account surplus for December fell 23.1 percent from a year earlier to 820.7 billion yen, while the surplus in merchandise trade alone decreased 20.0 percent to 1.046 trillion yen.
At Monday's exchange rate of about 122 yen to the dollar, the 1996 current account surplus was $58.8 billion and the surplus for December alone was $6.72 billion.

Economists polled by Reuters before the trade figures were released had forecast, on average, a 23 percent drop in the December current account surplus to around 817.2 billion yen, against 1.07 trillion yen a year earlier.

They said the pace of the long decline in the politically sensitive surplus was likely to slow in the coming months, with the trade surplus -- the core of the current account calculation -- expected to stop falling due to the weaker yen.

They had also predicted that the services deficit, another component of the current account data, would widen in December from a year earlier on an increase in the number of Japanese travelling abroad.
